assessments.title: Practise building fair and trustworthy capability systems
assessments.description: Apply software design and evidence principles to realistic decisions about assessments, verified access, merit, privacy, and student opportunities.
learning_objectives: Apply published access and attempt rules without bypassing payment verification.
Distinguish verified capability evidence from payment, participation, and unreviewed signals.
Design transparent, privacy-conscious opportunity workflows that do not promise awards.

questions.prompt: A product owner asks the team to award merit points whenever a student opens a paid practice assessment. Which design best preserves the difference between access and demonstrated capability?
options: Add points as soon as the payment reference is entered.
Award merit for opening the assessment, then subtract points for wrong answers.
Use verified assessment performance under published scoring rules for merit; treat payment only as an access condition.
Give more merit to students who pay for the largest number of attempts.
questions.correct_answer: Use verified assessment performance under published scoring rules for merit; treat payment only as an access condition.
questions.rationale: Payment can control access to a programme but is not evidence of capability. Merit must be grounded in verified performance and rules disclosed to students.

questions.prompt: A payment form accepts a student's M-Pesa reference. The gateway has not confirmed the transaction. What should happen before the assessment becomes startable?
options: The server should keep the request pending until authorized payment evidence is verified.
The browser should mark the payment verified when the reference has the right number of characters.
The assessment should unlock immediately and be relocked only if an administrator notices an issue.
A successful form submission should be treated as proof that funds were received.
questions.correct_answer: The server should keep the request pending until authorized payment evidence is verified.
questions.rationale: A submitted reference is a claim, not confirmation of funds. The backend should grant access only after an authorized verification decision and preserve an auditable record.

questions.prompt: A learner has a pending Sponsored View payment and sends a request directly to the assessment-start endpoint. Which response is appropriate?
options: Start the assessment because the payment reference is present.
Start a shortened assessment while the payment is checked.
Change the payment status to verified when the start request is received.
Deny the start until the KSh 20 payment is verified, and return a clear reason.
questions.correct_answer: Deny the start until the KSh 20 payment is verified, and return a clear reason.
questions.rationale: Access control must be enforced by the server, not by the frontend or by user-submitted payment details. A pending payment must not create an entitlement.

questions.prompt: An automated job processes Sponsored View payments close to midnight in East Africa Time. Which approach correctly enforces the five-attempt daily limit?
options: Count attempts using whichever time zone the student's browser reports.
Calculate the EAT calendar-day interval on the server and count qualifying attempts within that interval.
Reset the limit at an arbitrary UTC hour without converting the activity day.
Allow a sixth attempt and ask support to remove it later.
questions.correct_answer: Calculate the EAT calendar-day interval on the server and count qualifying attempts within that interval.
questions.rationale: The rule is defined by the East Africa Time calendar day. A server-calculated EAT interval avoids client clock manipulation and inconsistent boundary handling.

questions.prompt: A dashboard needs to tell a student their contest rank without disclosing other students' private results. Which response is the best fit?
options: Return every student's name, phone number, and exact score to each learner.
Show an invented rank until enough students participate.
Return the requesting student's calculated rank and cohort size, while limiting peer data to what the product intentionally publishes.
Hide the student's result and show only a generic success animation.
questions.correct_answer: Return the requesting student's calculated rank and cohort size, while limiting peer data to what the product intentionally publishes.
questions.rationale: Students need their own standing, but that does not justify exposing other participants' personal data or scores. The API can disclose a calculated rank and aggregate context.

questions.prompt: A support programme has no configured eligibility formula. A student finishes an assessment and asks whether they qualify. What should the platform do?
options: Invent a reasonable-looking cutoff and make an automatic award decision.
Show that eligibility cannot yet be determined because approved criteria are not configured.
Treat all students with a passing assessment score as eligible for every programme.
Use the student's payment amount as a replacement merit formula.
questions.correct_answer: Show that eligibility cannot yet be determined because approved criteria are not configured.
questions.rationale: Consequential eligibility decisions require approved, published rules. The system should identify missing configuration rather than inventing a cutoff or substituting payment.

questions.prompt: A content update changes a question after a student has started an assessment. Which implementation best protects a fair attempt?
options: Replace the question in the active attempt and grade the new version.
Let the student's browser submit an answer key for whichever version it prefers.
Delete the attempt and tell the student to pay again.
Keep an immutable question snapshot for the attempt and grade against that recorded version.
questions.correct_answer: Keep an immutable question snapshot for the attempt and grade against that recorded version.
questions.rationale: A snapshot makes the assessed content and answer key stable from start through grading. It supports fairness, auditability, and historical record preservation.

questions.prompt: An application needs an M-Pesa payment number and one programme-specific response. Which collection practice is most appropriate?
options: Collect only the payment details and programme information needed, protect them with access controls, and avoid exposing them in public endpoints.
Request identity documents, contacts, and account passwords in case they are useful later.
Display submitted payment numbers on a public leaderboard for transparency.
Store application details in a browser URL so an administrator can retrieve them.
questions.correct_answer: Collect only the payment details and programme information needed, protect them with access controls, and avoid exposing them in public endpoints.
questions.rationale: Data minimization reduces privacy risk. Sensitive application and payment details should be limited to necessary fields and accessible only to authorized student and administrative workflows.

questions.prompt: A student submits a support application and sees the status 'Submitted'. No administrator has reviewed it yet. Which dashboard message is accurate?
options: Your award has been approved and will be paid today.
Your application is recorded and awaiting review; payment is not confirmed.
Your application was declined because it is not already marked Paid.
Your leaderboard position guarantees the requested funding.
questions.correct_answer: Your application is recorded and awaiting review; payment is not confirmed.
questions.rationale: Submitted is a workflow state, not approval or payment confirmation. Status labels must reflect the actual administrative and funding decisions.

questions.prompt: A student qualifies for both a Sponsored View reward and a philanthropic support programme. How should the backend represent the claims?
options: Merge both into one generic payment record so their eligibility rules cannot differ.
Treat any qualifying leaderboard placement as proof that both payments were paid.
Keep distinct programme records with their own eligibility rules, funding state, application, and payment evidence.
Allow the student to edit both programme statuses from the dashboard.
questions.correct_answer: Keep distinct programme records with their own eligibility rules, funding state, application, and payment evidence.
questions.rationale: Different programmes can have different rules, funding, and review processes. Separate records support accurate decisions, traceability, and prevention of duplicate or unsupported payouts.
